clauses.reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 0-703 of the held text jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-8525-exemption-harry-t-edwards-from-compulsory-retirement-for-age.txt): signed August 26, 1940. The recital finds that the public interest requires that the employee be further exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year, and the operative sentence, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), further exempts Harry T. Edwards from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending October 31, 1941. That exemption is the order's only command and it carries its own fixed term. The recital names the earlier exemption Executive Order No. 8259 of September 21, 1939; those are earlier instruments, not events on this order. First end: the order's own stated end, October 31, 1941 (operative sentence: "for a period of one year ending October 31, 1941."). The stated date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of October 31, 1941); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when October 31, 1941 begins, is the alternative. The date is the end of the stated term, not a record of separation or death; no such record is held. Later event, not an end: Executive Order 8827, signed July 24, 1941, further exempts the same person; its recital names this order ("Executive Orders No. 8259 of September 21, 1939, and No. 8525 of August 26, 1940") and its operative sentence runs "ending October 31, 1941". Like this order it has no effective-date wording, so I read it as effective on signing. The period that EO 8827 states ends on the same day as the period of this order; a later order, EO 8844 of August 8, 1941, amends EO 8827 (not this order) so that its period ends October 31, 1942. EO 8844 does not name this order and is not an event on it; I read it because the name search listed it.

savings.reason: The exemption let Harry T. Edwards remain in service past the retirement age that would otherwise have required automatic separation; service rendered while the exemption ran is an accrued effect that remains after the stated end date. The order says nothing about any status, right or duty after October 31, 1941, so no independent continuing command or residual obligation of this order survives its stated term. Later service under the further exemption came from a separate order, not from this one.
